stem.en: In Thomson's model, an atom has 6 electrons spread through a sphere of positive charge. How much positive charge must the sphere carry, and why?

text.en: +6, because the atom is neutral, so the positive charge must equal the negative charge of the 6 electrons.
0, because electrons are the only charged particles in the atom.
+1, because the atom has only one positive sphere.

explanation.en: Each electron has a charge of -1, so 6 electrons give -6. The atom is neutral, so the sphere must carry +6, and +6 and -6 add up to zero. A sphere with no charge would leave the whole atom at -6, which is not neutral. There is one sphere, but one sphere can hold any amount of charge: it need not be +1.

hints.en: Add up the charge of the electrons first. What must the total for the atom be?
